name: THEMIS daytime infrared
description: Daytime infrared mosaic. Bright sun-facing slopes and dark shaded slopes reveal terrain and thermal contrast.
source: NASA Mars Trek / Mars Odyssey THEMIS
credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Arizona State University; USGS; NASA Mars Trek
coverage: Global mosaic with gaps; transparent pixels mean no data.
epoch: October 2018 controlled mosaic, version 2; multiple observation dates
limitation: Qualitative grayscale infrared brightness, not calibrated temperature. Illumination, season and surface properties affect contrast. Missing tiles are unavailable data, not zero temperature.

name: THEMIS nighttime infrared
description: Nighttime infrared mosaic. Thermal contrasts help distinguish surfaces that cool at different rates.
source: NASA Mars Trek / Mars Odyssey THEMIS
credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Arizona State University; USGS; NASA Mars Trek
coverage: Global mosaic with gaps; transparent pixels mean no data.
epoch: October 2018 controlled mosaic, version 2; multiple observation dates
limitation: Qualitative grayscale infrared brightness, not calibrated temperature or thermal inertia. Missing tiles are unavailable data, not zero temperature.

name: MOLA color relief
description: Elevation-colored shaded relief from Mars Global Surveyor laser altimetry.
source: NASA Mars Trek / Mars Global Surveyor MOLA
credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MOLA Science Team; USGS; NASA Mars Trek
coverage: Global tile grid; source observations span 88°S to 88°N. Polar fill is not measured coverage.
limitation: Qualitative elevation colors with hillshade. Legend swatches sample the rendered image and have no calibrated height values. This image cannot supply slope or elevation measurements. JPEG source has no no-data alpha mask.

name: TES surface albedo
description: Surface reflectivity measured by the TES visible and near-infrared detector. Broad bright and dark regions trace differences in surface materials.
source: NASA Mars Trek / Mars Global Surveyor TES
credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Arizona State University; TES Science Team; NASA Mars Trek
resolution: About 7,410 m/pixel source mosaic, 8 pixels/degree; served tiles are coarser
coverage: Global mosaic with masked pixels; transparent pixels mean no data.
epoch: Mars Global Surveyor mission archive; exact mosaic observation interval not supplied
limitation: Qualitative grayscale reflectivity. The tile service does not publish a calibrated pixel-to-albedo conversion. Broadband albedo does not identify minerals. Native service ends at level 1; enlargement adds no detail.

name: MOLA regional roughness
description: Regional vertical roughness from laser altimetry. Brightness shows general roughness; RGB hue compares roughness across spatial baselines.
source: NASA Mars Trek / Mars Global Surveyor MOLA
credit: NASA/MOLA Science Team; M. A. Kreslavsky and J. W. Head; NASA Mars Trek
resolution: About 7,500 m/pixel source map, 8 pixels/degree; served tiles are coarser
coverage: Global regional map; transparent pixels mean no data. Polar interpolation is not local ground truth.
epoch: MOLA mission archive; Kreslavsky and Head 2000 product cited by Mars Trek
limitation: Qualitative RGB composite, not a scalar color ramp. The legend describes brightness only. Trek assigns blue, green and red to 600 m, 2,400 m and 9,200 m baselines. This is not boulder-scale terrain or EVA walkability. Native service ends at level 1.

name: Global geologic map, SIM 3292
description: Geologic units mapped from orbit, colored by unit and age.
source: USGS SIM 3292 via NASA Mars Trek
credit: Tanaka et al. 2014, USGS SIM 3292; NASA Mars Trek
resolution: 1:20,000,000 map scale; units are tens to thousands of km across
epoch: Published 2014 from MGS, Odyssey, MEX and MRO data
limitation: Map units, not rock types at a site. Boundaries are drawn at 1:20M, so they can be kilometers off at EVA scale. Colors are categories, not a value scale.
